info.title: mimux API
info.summary: The REST API of the mimux pro layer — mail read, written and moved by a machine.
info.description:
mimux is a self-hosted, single-user mail client.

**The product line, in one sentence: a human driving mimux is free, a machine driving mimux is the paid pro layer.**

The mail client itself — multi-account unified inbox, IMAP IDLE sync, threading, search, compose, drafts, undo-send, scheduled send, filters, calendar invites, notifications, backup/restore, AI compose and translate with your own key — is AGPL-3.0 and always will be. Nothing is ever moved from the free side to the paid side.

This API is the other half: `pro/`, licensed under the [Elastic Licence 2.0](https://github.com/mattmezza/mimux/blob/main/pro/LICENSE). It is only compiled into the binary built with the `pro` build tag. The free binary does not contain it, and `make verify-free` proves that on every commit. See [LICENSING.md](https://github.com/mattmezza/mimux/blob/main/LICENSING.md).

## There is no central API host

mimux is software you run. Every install is its own API. The `servers` entry below is a template: substitute the origin of *your* mimux, e.g. `https://mail.example.com/api`. There is no shared hosted endpoint to point a client at, and there never will be — your mail stays on your machine.

## Conventions

- All field names are `snake_case`.
- All timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC (`2026-08-17T09:30:00Z`).
- Request bodies are JSON and reject unknown fields with `400 invalid_request`, so a typo fails loudly instead of being silently dropped. Bodies are capped at 32 MiB.
- Every non-2xx response is the same `Error` envelope: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`.
- Collections use `{"data": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}`. `next_cursor` is `""` when there is nothing left; endpoints that are not paginated still return the field, always as `""`.

## Authentication

A personal access token, minted in **Settings → API**, sent as `Authorization: Bearer mimux_pat_…`. Tokens carry scopes; every operation documents the scope it needs both in prose and in the `x-required-scope` extension. Revoking a token in Settings takes effect on the next request — the middleware re-reads the row every time.

## Rate limiting

Per token, token-bucket, refilling continuously to `MIMUX_API_RATE_LIMIT` requests per minute (default 120; set it to 0 to disable). Over budget is `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header in whole seconds. The limiter is in-process, so it resets when mimux restarts.

## Idempotency

`POST /v1/messages/send`, `POST /v1/drafts` and `POST /v1/filters` accept an `Idempotency-Key` header. A repeat of the same key by the same token on the same path replays the stored response byte-for-byte with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, so a retried send cannot go out twice.

Honest caveat: **the key store is in memory, per process.** Keys do not survive a restart, they expire after 24 hours, and when 1024 keys accumulate the whole store is dropped at once rather than evicted LRU. Treat it as at-most-once *per process lifetime*, not as a durable guarantee. Only 2xx responses are stored — a failed call is safe to re-execute.

## Webhooks

mimux can also POST to you. See the **Webhooks** tag for the outbound events, the signature scheme and a verification snippet, and `/v1/webhooks` for managing endpoints.

## MCP server

mimux pro is also an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, so agents that speak MCP get the same capabilities as this REST API without any glue code.

- **Endpoint:** `POST {your-mimux-host}/api/mcp` — stateless streamable HTTP. Every request is self-contained; there is no session to establish or expire.
- **Auth:** the same `Authorization: Bearer mimux_pat_...` tokens as the REST API, honouring the same scopes. `tools/list` reflects the token's scopes — a tool whose scope the token lacks simply is not offered.

| Tool | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `list_accounts` | `accounts:read` | sync state + unread counts |
| `list_folders` | `mail:read` | folder tree with ids |
| `search_mail` | `mail:read` | local index by default; `deep=true` asks the IMAP servers (~15s) |
| `read_message` | `mail:read` | chunked bodies with explicit `offset` continuation |
| `mark_read` | `mail:modify` |  |
| `star_message` | `mail:modify` |  |
| `move_message` | `mail:modify` | folder id or archive/spam/trash; trash requires `confirm=true` |
| `draft_reply` | `mail:send` | creates a real draft + preview; **does not send** |
| `send_draft` | `mail:send` | the only tool that sends; two-step by design |

There is also a `mimux://inbox/summary` resource (unified inbox summary as JSON, requires `mail:read`).

**stdio bridge:** MCP clients that only speak stdio run `mimux mcp` (pro builds only) with `MIMUX_URL` (default `http://localhost:8083`) and `MIMUX_TOKEN` in the environment. The bridge proxies to a running mimux's `/api/mcp` — it never opens the database itself.

A complete worked example — an agent that triages an inbox over this endpoint — lives in `examples/triage/` in the repository.

## Licence

The pro layer verifies a signed licence key offline — there is no phone-home, no activation call and no machine fingerprint. Set it with `MIMUX_LICENCE_KEY` (which wins) or paste it into **Settings → Licence**; `mimux licence status` prints what the running build makes of it and exits non-zero when the API is paused.

Without a covering licence, **every operation below answers `402` with the `licence_required` or `licence_version` code** (see the `LicenceRequired` response). Two endpoints never do: `GET /health` and `GET /v1/openapi.json` are open unconditionally. Nothing in the mail client is affected either — sync, send, search and the web UI are AGPL code that has no licence check in it at all.

- **Trial.** A pro build with no key runs for 14 days from its first boot. Responses carry `X-Mimux-Trial: <n> days left`.
- **Grace.** An expired annual licence keeps serving for 45 more days, and every response carries `X-Mimux-Licence-Warning: licence expired <date>; API stops <date>`.
- **Perpetual.** A perpetual licence covers builds up to its watermark version, forever. Running a *newer* build is `402 licence_version`, naming both versions — never a silent degrade.

servers.description: Your own mimux install. mimux is self-hosted: there is no shared or central API host, so this URL is a template you fill in with the origin you serve mimux from.

your-mimux-host.description: Scheme and host of your mimux instance, without a trailing slash — e.g. https://mail.example.com, or http://localhost:8080 in development. The API is always mounted under /api on the same origin as the web client.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Two things live under this tag: the endpoints you manage over `/v1/webhooks`, and the outbound events those endpoints receive (listed at the end of this document, under **Webhooks**).

mimux POSTs a small JSON body to your URL when something happens, so an agent does not have to poll. Each endpoint has its own signing secret, shown once, when it is created.

## The request

```http
POST /your/url HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: mimux-webhooks/1
X-Mimux-Event: message.received
X-Mimux-Delivery-Id: 4f8c1d0e5b7a2c9f3e1d6a8b0c4f7e21
X-Mimux-Signature: t=1700000000,v1=79883357e4c4c4abee43cf4b32367d67a1344520479e3e8c85e98406a6d6a2a5
```

The body is always the same envelope — `id`, `event`, `created_at`, `data` — where `id` is the same value as the `X-Mimux-Delivery-Id` header. **Payloads are summaries: a message body is never sent.**

## Verifying the signature

`v1` is `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")`, hex-encoded. Verify it against the exact bytes you received, before parsing any JSON, and reject a stale timestamp: `t` is inside the signed string, so a captured delivery cannot be re-stamped and replayed at you later.

```python
import hashlib, hmac, time

def verify(secret: str, header: str, raw_body: bytes) -> bool:
    parts = dict(p.split('=', 1) for p in header.split(','))
    t, v1 = parts['t'], parts['v1']
    if abs(time.time() - int(t)) > 300:            # reject replays
        return False
    signed = f'{t}.'.encode() + raw_body            # timestamp, dot, raw body
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), signed, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, v1)       # constant time
```

Answer `2xx` once you have accepted the delivery. Answer `410 Gone` if you never want it again.

## Delivery semantics

- **At least once.** A delivery that times out is retried even if you did process it, so deduplicate on `X-Mimux-Delivery-Id` — it is stable across every retry and every replay.
- Retry ladder: immediately, then after 1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 8h and 14h. Seven attempts over roughly a day. Timeouts, `5xx`, `429` and the other `4xx` are all retried (a misconfigured receiver is usually misconfigured temporarily); `410 Gone` is not — that delivery dies at once.
- When one delivery exhausts the whole ladder the **endpoint is auto-disabled**: `active` goes `false` and `auto_disabled_at` is stamped. `PATCH` it back to `active: true` when the receiver is fixed; that clears the stamp.
- 10 second timeout per attempt, at most 2 redirects followed, `http`/`https` URLs only.
- Deliveries queued while an endpoint is paused stay queued; they go out when it is switched back on.
- The last 100 deliveries per endpoint are kept and readable, and any of them can be replayed.

## Honest caveats

- **Only the pro binary delivers.** The free build shows the same Settings UI and stores what you configure there — and never posts anything. The endpoints are inert until you run pro.
- `message.received` and `message.sent` ride on IMAP sync, which is what bounds them: an account announces nothing until it has completed one successful sync in this process (that is what keeps a first sync from replaying months of mail at you), and nothing whose IMAP `INTERNALDATE` is over a day old.
- `message.sent` is the Sent-folder copy of an outgoing message, so it fires when that copy syncs back — moments after SMTP accepted it, not at the instant it did.
- Events are not ordered relative to each other, and nothing that happened while mimux was stopped is replayed when it starts.

get.description:
Unauthenticated on purpose: a health probe that needs a credential is a health probe nobody wires up. It exposes a count of configured accounts and nothing else — no mail, no addresses, no account names.

Note the path: this one lives at `/api/health`, **not** under `/api/v1`.

Serves the OpenAPI description of the running binary, embedded at compile time. Unauthenticated: it is public documentation, and a client that cannot yet authenticate is exactly the client that needs to read it.

Returns the label and scopes of the token that authenticated the request.

**Scope: none.** Scope-free by design — it tells a client what its own credential may do, which is exactly what a client holding a too-narrow token needs in order to find that out.

Every configured account, with its live sync state and stored-mail counters.

Not paginated: `next_cursor` is always `""`.

**Scope: `accounts:read`.**

Returns one entry per account, each holding that account's folder tree. IMAP delimiters are turned into nesting, so `Work/Clients/Acme` becomes three levels. Intermediate path segments that have no folder of their own carry only a `label` — no `id`, and they cannot be listed or moved to.

Not paginated: `next_cursor` is always `""`.

Honest caveat: an `account` that does not exist is not a 404 — it returns an entry with an empty `folders` array.

**Scope: `mail:read`.**

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: Narrow to a single account by name. Omitted, every configured account is returned.

200.description: Folder trees, one entry per account.

get.description:
Messages newest-first, from the local store — this never touches IMAP.

**Scope selection**, in order: `folder` if given, else the inbox of `account`, else the unified inbox (every account's inbox folder).

**Pagination is by conversation, not by row.** A page holds every message of the `limit` conversations whose newest message falls in its band, so a page boundary can never cut a thread in half — which also means a page can contain *more* than `limit` messages. Additionally, the first page (no `cursor`) keeps every unread conversation however old it is, so a client that only reads page one still sees all its unread mail.

**Cursor semantics.** `next_cursor` is an opaque string; pass it back as `cursor` for the next page. Structurally it is `<rfc3339-date>_<message-id>` of the newest message of the last conversation delivered, which makes it stable against the list mutating underneath you — a sync inserting at the top or an archive removing from the middle cannot make you skip or repeat rows the way an offset would. Stop when `next_cursor` comes back `""`.

**Filters are applied to each fetched page, not to the query.** `unread`, `starred`, `since`, `from`, `to` and `subject` are evaluated after the page is read, so a filtered response can hold far fewer than `limit` items — including zero — while more matches still exist further down. Keep following `next_cursor` until it is empty. For anything more expressive, use `POST /v1/messages/search`, which speaks the full query language.

Each item is annotated with `thread_id` and `thread_size` (whole-conversation size, which may exceed what is on the page). Those two fields appear only here — search results do not carry them.

**Scope: `mail:read`.**

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Folder id to list. Takes precedence over `account`. Unknown id is a 404.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: Account name; lists that account's inbox. Ignored when `folder` is given. An account with no inbox folder is a 404.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Conversations per page. Out of range is a 400 — it is not clamped.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page. Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description: `true`/`1` keeps only unread messages; `false`/`0` keeps only read ones. Any other value (including `yes`) is ignored and the filter is not applied.

parameters.name: starred
parameters.description: `true`/`1` keeps only starred messages; `false`/`0` keeps only unstarred ones. Same lenient parsing as `unread`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Keep messages dated at or after this RFC 3339 instant. Honest caveat: a value that does not parse as RFC 3339 is silently ignored rather than rejected.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the sender's display name and address, joined by a space.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the To and Cc address lists, joined by a space.

get.description:
Full metadata plus the body forms you ask for, plus the attachment manifest.

The body is fetched from IMAP (through the client's body cache). If that fails — the account is offline, the message is gone from the server — the request still succeeds: `body` is omitted and `body_error` explains. That is deliberate, so an agent can always read metadata even while sync is broken.

The `html` form is the same sanitized document the reading pane renders, with one difference: external images are left in place, because the caller is a machine reading JSON rather than a browser that would leak a read receipt. Active content is still stripped.

`attachments` is always present, `[]` when the message has none — or when listing them failed, which is not reported separately.

`thread_id` and `thread_size` are not set on this endpoint.

**Scope: `mail:read`.**

patch.summary: Change read, star, labels or folder
patch.description:
Applies every field present in the body, in order: read, starred, labels added, labels removed, folder move. Omitted fields are left alone.

Writes land in the local store immediately and the IMAP side effect follows in the background — the same optimistic pattern as the web client, minus its 11-second undo window: an API caller that asks for a move means it, so the server-side move fires at once. A background IMAP failure is logged, not returned; flag writes are also retried by the sync loop's dirty sweep.

`folder_id` must belong to the same account as the message; cross-account moves are a 400. Moving to the folder the message is already in is a no-op.

The response is the message re-read from the store after all changes, without `thread_id`/`thread_size`.

**Scope: `mail:modify`.**

delete.description:
Moves the message to the account's `trash` special-use folder. **Nothing is erased** — this is the client's Delete, which is a move. There is no API for permanent deletion.

Store first, IMAP move in the background, no undo window. An account without a trash folder is a 400 and the message stays put.

**Scope: `mail:modify`.**

post.description:
Moves the message to the account's `archive` special-use folder. Store first, IMAP move in the background, no undo window. An account without an archive folder is a 400 and the message stays put.

Takes no request body.

**Scope: `mail:modify`.**

Moves the message to the account's `spam` special-use folder. Store first, IMAP move in the background, no undo window. An account without a spam folder is a 400 and the message stays put.

Takes no request body.

**Scope: `mail:modify`.**

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Zero-based attachment index, exactly the `index` field from `GET /v1/messages/{id}`. Indices are positional within that response and are not stable across re-fetches of a rewritten message.

get.description:
Streams the raw attachment bytes with its real media type (falling back to `application/octet-stream`), `Content-Disposition: attachment` carrying the filename, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

This one reaches IMAP, so it fails when the account is offline: `502 upstream`.

**Scope: `mail:read`.**

Content-Disposition.description: `attachment; filename="..."`. Any double quotes in the filename are stripped.

404.description: No such message, or `n` is negative or beyond the attachment count.

post.description:
Runs a query in mimux's own search language.

**Query language.** Whitespace-separated terms, ANDed; there is no OR. Double quotes keep a phrase together. A leading `-` negates a term, but only when what follows is a real operator — `-word` is just a word. Operators: `from:`, `to:`, `cc:`, `subject:`, `body:`, `in:`, `label:`, `is:unread|read|starred`, `has:attachment|link`, `before:YYYY-MM-DD`, `after:YYYY-MM-DD`, `larger:`/`smaller:` with a size like `5mb`, `100kb`, `512`. Anything else — including an operator with an unparseable value — degrades to a bare free-text term rather than erroring. A query that parses to zero terms is a `400 invalid_request`.

**`mode: "local"`** (the default) searches the synced SQLite index synchronously and returns results in the collection envelope. `next_cursor` is always `""` — local search is not paginated, it is capped by `limit`.

**`mode: "deep"`** asks the IMAP servers themselves, which is slow, so it returns `202` with a job you poll at `GET /v1/search/jobs/{id}`. See that endpoint for the job lifecycle and its caveats.

`scope` defaults by what else you sent: `folder` if `folder_id` is set, else `account` if `account` is set, else `all`. (The web client defaults to `account`; the API defaults to `all`, so a bare query means "everywhere".)

Results do not carry `thread_id`/`thread_size`.

**Scope: `mail:read`** — deep search included, because it only reads.

202.description: Deep search accepted; poll the job.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The job id returned by a deep search.

get.description:
Returns the job; `results` appears once `status` is `done`.

**Honest caveats on the job lifecycle — this part is deliberately minimal:**

- There are only two statuses, `running` and `done`. **There is no failure state.** Deep search fans out per account with a per-account timeout; a folder whose IMAP search errors or times out simply contributes nothing. A job whose every account failed still finishes `done` with an empty `results`, indistinguishable from a query that genuinely matched nothing.
- There is no progress indicator, no result count while running, and no way to cancel.
- **Jobs live in memory only, in a ring of the 32 most recent.** They vanish on restart, and job 33 evicts job 1. Polling either afterwards is a `404`, whose message says so.
- An identical query repeated within 10 minutes is answered from the result cache and comes back `done` immediately, without touching IMAP.
- Envelopes for hits are cached into the local store as a side effect, so a deep search makes those messages available to local search afterwards.

Poll at a sane interval; there is no long-poll or webhook (webhooks do not exist yet).

**Scope: `mail:read`.**

404.description: No such job — unknown id, evicted from the 32-job ring, or lost to a restart.

error.message: No such search job (jobs are kept in memory and expire on restart).

post.summary: Send a message, now or later
post.description:
Builds and sends a message over the account's SMTP, or — when `schedule_at` is set — enqueues it in the outbox for the scheduler to send at that time.

**Sending account resolution**, in order, with no guessing: explicit `account`; else the account owning the `from` address; else the account of the message named by `in_reply_to`; else the only configured account if there is exactly one. Anything ambiguous is a `400`.

**Threading.** `in_reply_to` takes a mimux **message id** (an integer), not a `Message-ID` header value. The `In-Reply-To` and `References` headers are derived from that message exactly the way the compose form derives them.

**Attachments** are inline base64 in the request body, capped at 25 MiB in total; the whole request body is capped at 32 MiB.

Send it with an `Idempotency-Key` header — a retry after a timeout is exactly the case this endpoint exists to survive. See the API description for what that guarantee is and is not.

**Scope: `mail:send`.**

202.description: Queued for `schedule_at`. Cancelling or editing a scheduled message is only possible in the web client today; there is no API for the outbox.

error.message: in_reply_to: no message with that id.

502.description: SMTP refused or was unreachable. The underlying error text is included verbatim — this is a single-user install and the operator owns both ends of that conversation.

error.message: Send failed: dial tcp: connection refused

post.description:
Stores a draft — the same row the compose form autosaves into, so a draft created here opens in the web client.

Note the shape difference against `POST /v1/messages/send`: recipients here are **single comma-separated strings**, not arrays, because that is how the compose form stores them.

`in_reply_to` takes a mimux message id and is resolved to that message's `Message-ID` header on the way in; it also fills `account` when you left it blank. `kind` defaults to `new`.

Honest caveat: there is no `GET /v1/drafts` or `DELETE /v1/drafts/{id}` yet. You can create and update; listing and deleting are web-client-only.

**Scope: `mail:send`** — a draft is unsent mail, so it follows the sending scope rather than `mail:modify`.

patch.description:
Merges the provided fields into an existing draft. Fields you leave out keep their stored value; a field set to `""` clears it. `kind` and `in_reply_to` cannot be changed after creation.

Not idempotency-keyed — a repeated PATCH is naturally idempotent.

**Scope: `mail:send`.**

get.description:
Every stored rule, in no guaranteed order beyond what the store returns (rules carry a `position` that decides evaluation order).

Not paginated: `next_cursor` is always `""`.

**Scope: `mail:read`** — filters govern how mail is handled, so they follow the mail scopes rather than getting one of their own.

post.description:
Validates and stores a rule. Any `id` in the body is ignored and overwritten by the assigned one.

Validation is strict and happens before the write: a name is required, at least one condition and at least one action are required, condition fields and operators must be known, values must be non-empty, and a `regex` condition must actually compile. Failures come back as `400 invalid_request` with the validator's own message.

Rules apply to incoming mail during sync. Creating one does not re-run it over existing mail.

Honest caveat: there is no update or delete endpoint for filters yet — creating and listing is the whole surface.

**Scope: `mail:modify`.**

get.description:
Every configured endpoint, newest first. The signing secret is **not** included — it is returned once, by the create call, and never again.

Not paginated: `next_cursor` is always `""`.

**Scope: `webhooks:manage`.**

post.description:
Registers a URL and generates its signing secret. **The secret is in this response and in no other**: store it now, because nothing returns it again — to change it, delete the endpoint and create another.

`url` must be an absolute `http`/`https` URL; anything else is a `400`. Unknown event names are dropped silently, so check the `events` you get back. An endpoint subscribed to nothing is legal and simply never fires (a test delivery still works — see the test endpoint).

**Scope: `webhooks:manage`.**

201.description: Created. The one and only sighting of the secret.

patch.description:
Merges the provided fields; absent ones keep their stored value. `events` replaces the whole subscription list rather than adding to it.

Setting `active: true` also clears `auto_disabled_at` — switching an endpoint back on is how you say the receiver is fixed. There is no way to rotate the secret: delete and re-create.

**Scope: `webhooks:manage`.**

delete.description:
Removes the endpoint, its secret and its delivery log. Anything still queued for it is dropped.

**Scope: `webhooks:manage`.**

get.description:
The endpoint's recent deliveries, newest first: what was sent, how it went, and when the next attempt is due. The payload itself is not included — read it from your own receiver, or replay the delivery.

The log is bounded at the write end: the last 100 deliveries per endpoint are kept, older rows are pruned as new ones arrive. That is why there is no cursor here and `next_cursor` is always `""`.

**Scope: `webhooks:manage`.**

parameters.name: did
parameters.description: The delivery's `id` from the log — the row id, not the `delivery_id` string sent on the wire.

post.description:
Re-queues the delivery for immediate sending with a fresh retry budget. The body and the `delivery_id` are unchanged, so a receiver that already processed it recognises the duplicate — only the signature's timestamp differs, because it is computed per attempt.

Use it after fixing a receiver that was returning `500`, or to re-deliver something you lost. Sending happens in the background; this call returns as soon as the row is queued.

**Scope: `webhooks:manage`.**

Queues a `ping` delivery to this endpoint and sends it immediately — the way to prove the URL, the signature check and your parser all work without waiting for real mail.

`ping` ignores the subscription list on purpose: an endpoint subscribed to nothing still receives its test. It is also not a subscribable event, which is why you will not find it in `events`.

It goes through the normal machinery, so a `ping` that fails walks the same retry ladder and can auto-disable the endpoint like any other delivery. Watch the outcome in the delivery log.

**Scope: `webhooks:manage`.**

202.description: Queued; sending happens in the background.

post.description:
A message arrived in an account's **inbox** and was stored locally. Sent, archived and filed copies do not fire this — the Sent copy fires `message.sent`, and everything else fires nothing.

Rides on IMAP sync, so it is silent during a first sync and for anything over a day old. The payload is a summary; fetch the body with `GET /v1/messages/{id}` if you need it.

data.subject: Re: the analytical engine
data.snippet: I have been thinking about the ordering of operations…

410.description: Gone — this delivery is not retried. Use it to say you are done with these.

default.description: Anything else (including a timeout) is retried on the ladder, and a delivery that exhausts it auto-disables the endpoint.

post.description: A message left this mailbox: the copy in the account's **Sent** folder was stored. That copy is what fires this, so the event lands moments after SMTP accepted the message rather than at the instant it did — and an account whose Sent folder is not synced never fires it.

410.description: Gone — this delivery is not retried. Use it to say you are done with these.

default.description: Anything else (including a timeout) is retried on the ladder, and a delivery that exhausts it auto-disables the endpoint.

post.description:
An account's sync went into the error state — bad credentials, an expired OAuth token, a refused connection. This is the same text the status bar shows.

It fires on the **edge**: once when the account breaks, again only if the reason changes. A recovery is not announced (there is no `sync.ok`); poll `GET /v1/accounts` if you need to know when it clears.

410.description: Gone — this delivery is not retried. Use it to say you are done with these.

post.description:
A deep-search job started with `POST /v1/messages/search` (`mode: deep`) has finished. It carries the count, not the results — fetch those with `GET /v1/search/jobs/{id}`, which is also where the job's caveats are documented (in-memory, 32-job ring, no failure state).

This is the event that saves the most polling: a deep search answers long after its own HTTP response.

bearerAuth.description:
A mimux personal access token, minted in **Settings → API** and shown exactly once at creation. It always starts with `mimux_pat_`; a bearer value without that prefix is rejected without so much as a hash comparison.

```
Authorization: Bearer mimux_pat_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
```

Tokens are stored as argon2id hashes, may carry an expiry, and can be revoked from Settings — revocation is honoured on the very next request, because the middleware re-reads the token row every time.

**Scopes** are a space-separated subset of:

| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `mail:read` | Read mail: folders, messages, bodies, attachments, search, filters list. |
| `mail:send` | Send mail and manage drafts. |
| `mail:modify` | Change mail: read/star flags, labels, moves, archive/spam/trash, create filters. |
| `accounts:read` | Read the account list. |
| `webhooks:manage` | Manage webhook endpoints and their delivery log, including replaying a delivery and sending a test one. Reading them needs it too: a list of endpoints is a list of places this mailbox already talks to. |

A token created with no recognised scope falls back to `mail:read`. Call `GET /v1/tokens/self` to find out what the token in your hand actually holds.

WebhookID.name: id
WebhookID.description: The webhook endpoint id. A non-numeric or unknown value is a `404`.

MessageID.name: id
MessageID.description: The mimux message id — a local integer, not the RFC 5322 `Message-ID` header. A non-numeric value is a `404`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Any client-chosen string. Repeating it replays the stored 2xx response with `Idempotency-Replayed: true` instead of performing the action again. Keys are scoped to the calling token and the exact method and path, so two clients cannot collide on a generic key. In-memory, per process — see the API description for what that does and does not guarantee.

RetryAfter.description: Whole seconds to wait before the next request from this token will be admitted.

IdempotencyReplayed.description: Present and set to `true` only when this response was replayed from the idempotency store rather than freshly produced.

BadRequest.description: `invalid_request` — a malformed body (including an unknown JSON field), a parameter out of range, or a request the current state cannot satisfy, such as archiving in an account that has no archive folder.

Unauthorized.description: `unauthorized` — no `Authorization: Bearer` header, a value that is not a `mimux_pat_` token, or a token that is unknown, revoked or expired. The two cases are not distinguished in the message on purpose.

error.message: Missing or malformed Authorization header. Send: Authorization: Bearer <token>.

LicenceRequired.description: `licence_required` or `licence_version` — this install has no licence covering it (expired past its grace period, trial over, or a perpetual licence watermarked below this build). Only `/v1/*` and `/api/mcp` are affected: mail keeps syncing and sending, and `/health` and `/v1/openapi.json` keep answering. `details.url` is where to get a licence.

error.message: This licence expired on 2026-07-01 and its 45-day grace period ended on 2026-08-15, so the API and MCP endpoints are paused. Renew at https://account.mimux.dev. Your mail keeps syncing and sending as normal.

version.summary: Perpetual licence does not cover this build

error.message: This perpetual licence covers mimux up to v0.19; this build is v0.20. Renew at https://account.mimux.dev to cover v0.20, or run v0.19. Mail itself keeps working either way.

Forbidden.description: `insufficient_scope` — the token authenticated but does not carry the scope this operation needs. The message names the missing scope, so you know which box to tick in Settings → API.

error.message: This token is missing the mail:modify scope.

NotFound.description: `not_found` — no such resource, or a path id that is not an integer.

RateLimited.description: `rate_limited` — this token has spent its per-minute budget. `Retry-After` says how long to wait. The bucket refills continuously, so the wait is usually under a second.

error.message: Too many requests for this token. Retry in 3s.

InternalError.description: `internal` — mimux failed on its own side. Details are logged, never returned.

Upstream.description: `upstream` — the IMAP server could not be reached or refused. Usually means the account is offline; retry once sync recovers.

Error.description: The envelope of every non-2xx response, so a client can parse failures without special-casing per endpoint.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Branch on this, not on the message.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Wording may change between versions.

details.description: Extra context, present only on the codes that have somewhere to point you: the licence errors carry `url`.

NextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `""` when the collection is exhausted. Endpoints that are not paginated always return `""`.

accounts.description: Number of accounts with a running sync worker.

label.description: The name given to this token in Settings → API.

scopes.description: The scopes this token carries. `null` for the pathological case of a token whose scope string is empty.

Account.description: A configured account. Credentials — passwords, OAuth secrets, server hostnames — are never included.

name.description: The account's name, used wherever an `account` parameter is accepted.

state.description: Live sync state. Absent when the account has no running worker.

message.description: Detail accompanying `state`, typically the error when `state` is `error`. Absent when empty.

last_sync.description: Last *successful* sync, UTC. Absent until the account has synced once.

Folder.description: A node of the folder tree. A node that exists only as a path segment (an IMAP parent that holds no mail of its own) carries `label` and `children` and nothing else — in particular no `id`, so it cannot be listed or moved to.

label.description: The last path segment, as displayed.

id.description: Folder id. Absent on path-only nodes.

name.description: The full IMAP folder name, e.g. `Work/Clients/Acme`.

special_use.description: The folder's role, when it has one. Drives archive/spam/trash moves.

name.description: Display name. Absent when the header had none.

Message.description: A message as stored locally. Bodies and attachments are not here — fetch `GET /v1/messages/{id}` for those.

id.description: mimux's own id. This is what every `{id}` path and `in_reply_to` field takes.

message_id.description: The RFC 5322 `Message-ID` header. Absent when the message had none.

in_reply_to.description: The `In-Reply-To` header value. Absent when the message had none.

to.description: Recipient addresses, split from the stored header list. `null` — not `[]` — when there were none.

date.description: The message date, normalised to UTC.

snippet.description: Short preview extracted at sync time.

labels.description: Absent when the message has none.

thread_id.description: Id of the conversation's root message. **Set only by `GET /v1/messages`** — absent from single-message responses and from search results.

thread_size.description: Messages in the whole conversation, which may exceed how many of them are on this page. Same restriction as `thread_id`.

body.description: Present only when the body was fetched successfully. Which sub-fields appear depends on the `body` query parameter.

text.description: Plain-text body. Absent when not requested or empty.

html.description: Sanitized HTML body — active content stripped, external images left intact. Absent when not requested or empty.

body_error.description: Present instead of `body` when the body could not be fetched, typically because the account is offline. The request still succeeds with 200 and full metadata.

attachments.description: Always present; `[]` when the message has no attachments, and also `[]` if listing them failed.

index.description: Zero-based position in this list. Pass it as `{n}` to the attachment download endpoint.

MessagePatch.description: Every field is optional; only what is present is applied. Unknown fields are rejected with a 400.

read.description: Set or clear the read flag.

folder_id.description: Move the message here. Must belong to the same account as the message.
The folder the message now lives in.

SendRequest.description: Unknown fields are rejected with a 400.

account.description: Send from this account by name. Highest-priority way to resolve the sender.

from.description: The From address. Used to resolve the account when `account` is absent; must belong to a configured account. Defaults to the resolved account's own address.

to.description: Recipients. At least one is required.

mode.description: `markdown` is rendered to HTML with a plain-text alternative, the same way the compose form does it.

in_reply_to.description: A mimux **message id** to reply to — not a header value. Its `Message-ID` and `References` become this message's threading headers, and it can resolve the sending account.

attachments.description: Combined decoded size is capped at 25 MiB.

schedule_at.description: Send at this instant instead of now, via the outbox. Answers 202 rather than 200. A time in the past is not rejected — the scheduler picks it up on its next tick.

content_type.description: Media type. Left to the message builder when empty.

message_id.description: The RFC 5322 `Message-ID` header generated for the sent message — a header value, not a mimux id.

outbox_id.description: Outbox row id. There is no API to read, edit or cancel the outbox yet.

to.description: Comma-separated addresses, stored as one string.

kind.description: How the draft was started. Absent when empty.

DraftCreate.description: Unknown fields are rejected with a 400. Recipients are comma-separated strings here, unlike `SendRequest`.

account.description: Filled from `in_reply_to`'s message when left blank.

in_reply_to.description: A mimux message id, resolved to that message's `Message-ID` header for threading when the draft is eventually sent.

DraftPatch.description: Only the fields present are changed. `kind` and `in_reply_to` are not patchable; sending an unknown field is a 400.

SearchRequest.description: Unknown fields are rejected with a 400.

query.description: A query in mimux's search language. Must parse to at least one term.

scope.description: Where to search. Defaults to `folder` if `folder_id` is set, else `account` if `account` is set, else `all`. An unrecognised value falls back to `account`.

mode.description: `local` searches the synced index and answers 200. `deep` searches the IMAP servers and answers 202 with a job. Any other value is a 400.

limit.description: Local search only. Zero or negative means the default; anything above 500 is silently clamped to 500 rather than rejected.

SearchJob.description: An asynchronous deep search. Held in memory in a 32-job ring — see `GET /v1/search/jobs/{id}` for the caveats.

status.description: There is no failure status: a job whose IMAP searches all errored still ends `done`, with empty `results`.

results.description: Present only once `status` is `done`. Messages carry no `thread_id`/`thread_size`.

Filter.description: An auto-filter rule. All conditions must match (AND); there is no OR. A rule with no conditions never matches, which is why at least one is required.

id.description: Assigned on create; ignored if you send one.

account.description: Restrict to one account. Empty means every account.

op.description: `contains` is case-insensitive substring. `regex` is Go's RE2 syntax and must compile at write time.

type.description: `notify` takes no argument — what a notification says and where it goes is configured once in Settings → Notifications, not per rule.

arg.description: The action's argument where it takes one: the target folder for `move`, the address for `forward`, the label for `label`. Absent when empty.

Webhook.description: A configured endpoint. The signing secret is deliberately absent — it exists in the create response and nowhere else.

url.description: Absolute `http`/`https` URL. Anything else is refused on the way in.

events.description: What this endpoint is subscribed to. Empty is legal and means it never fires (a test delivery still works).

active.description: `false` means nothing is delivered. Queued deliveries wait rather than being dropped.

auto_disabled_at.description: Present when the engine switched this endpoint off after a delivery exhausted the retry ladder. `PATCH active: true` clears it.

events.description: Unknown names are dropped rather than rejected; check what comes back.

WebhookPatch.description: Every field is optional; absent ones keep their stored value. `events` replaces the whole list.

secret.description: The HMAC signing secret. Shown here once; no other response ever contains it.

note.description: The same warning in prose, so a client that dumps this response shows it to a human.

WebhookEventName.description: A subscribable event. `ping` is not one: it is only sent by the test endpoint.

WebhookDelivery.description: One event queued for one endpoint, plus the outcome so far. Kept for the last 100 deliveries per endpoint.

id.description: Row id — what you pass to the replay endpoint.

delivery_id.description: What the receiver sees as `X-Mimux-Delivery-Id`. Stable across retries and replays; deduplicate on it.

event.description: Event type, including `ping` for test deliveries.

status.description: `pending` queued, `failed` attempted with retries left, `ok` delivered, `dead` given up on (ladder exhausted, or the receiver said `410 Gone`).

attempts.description: Attempts made so far, out of the ladder's seven.

last_status_code.description: HTTP status of the last attempt. Absent when the request never got an answer.

last_error.description: Transport error from the last attempt, truncated. Absent when the last attempt reached the receiver.

WebhookEnvelope.description: The body of every outbound delivery. `data` is shaped by `event`.

id.description: The delivery id, identical to the `X-Mimux-Delivery-Id` header.

created_at.description: When the event happened — not when this attempt was made.

MessageReceivedData.description: A summary of the message. There is no body field, by design: a webhook is where mail leaves this machine without anyone watching.

id.description: mimux message id — fetch the full message with `GET /v1/messages/{id}`.

folder.description: IMAP folder name it landed in.

snippet.description: The same short preview the message list shows. Cheap: it was already stored.

to.description: Recipients as stored on the Sent copy. Bcc is not in it, because it is not in the message.

error.description: The failure as the status bar shows it. Wording comes from the IMAP layer and is not a stable machine-readable code.

results.description: Number of matches. Zero can also mean every account's IMAP search failed — deep-search jobs have no failure state.
